title: research-dossier IR
description: The intermediate representation between finished research and every renderer. The LLM authors this from a prose corpus; bin/research-dossier-render.mjs consumes it and never mutates it. Shape is enforced here; the referential and semantic rules a schema cannot express (source_claims resolve to real claim ids, truncated axes are declared, confidence is not asserted without a source) are enforced by the provenance gate in the renderer. Both must pass.

schema_version.description: SemVer of THIS contract, so a stored IR outlives the renderer that wrote it. Absent is treated as 1.0.0.

question.description: The one question this dossier answers. Not a topic — a question. 'Which chart library should we adopt?' not 'chart libraries'. A dossier that cannot state its question has no criterion for what belongs in it.

as_of.description: The date the corpus was current. Dossier-level; individual claims may be older (see claim.as_of) but never newer.

audience.description: Drives design-system selection and density (see references/audience-map.md). NOT cosmetic: it changes which parameters reach dataviz.

stakes.description: high tightens the gate: every claim must be confidence>=medium OR explicitly flagged in not_checked.

title.description: Optional display title. Defaults to question.

summary.description: Executive summary prose. Every factual assertion here SHOULD trace to a claim; the gate warns on numerals present in summary but absent from any claim.

entities.description: The things being described or compared — tools, vendors, cohorts, periods. Chart series and scorecard options reference these by id, so color follows the ENTITY and never its rank (dataviz non-negotiable).

claims.description: The atomic evidential units. EVERYTHING downstream — charts, scorecard cells, recommendations — cites these by id. A number that appears in a chart but in no claim is unsourced by construction, which is exactly what the provenance gate exists to catch.

scorecard.description: Present only for comparisons. See references/scorecard.md.

charts.description: Chart SPECIFICATIONS, not rendered charts. Form and color follow the bundled dataviz skill (cited, never copied): pick the form from the data's job, assign color by job, validate the palette by running the script.

insights.description: What the evidence means. Distinct from claims (what the evidence IS) — an insight is an interpretation and must cite the claims it rests on.

gaps.description: Known holes in the evidence — a question the corpus raised but did not answer. Distinct from not_checked (what was never looked at).

items.description: severity maps to the dataviz status palette, which always ships icon + label — a status color never carries meaning alone.

recommendations.description: The actionable output. owner and eta are REQUIRED: a recommendation with no owner and no date is a wish, and this format refuses to render wishes as decisions.

owner.description: A ROLE by preference (e.g. 'backend lead'), not a personal name — dossiers travel further than the people in them.

not_checked.description: REQUIRED and non-empty. The blind spots: what this research did NOT examine, and why. An empty array is not a passing state — it is a claim of omniscience, and the gate rejects it. If nothing was left unchecked, say so explicitly with a reason (e.g. 'scope was fully enumerable: only 3 candidate libraries exist').

reason.description: Why not — out of scope / no data / time-boxed / access denied.

impact.description: How much the missing evidence could change the conclusion. 'high' with stakes=high is a gate WARN: the dossier is admitting its own conclusion may not hold.

methodology.description: How the corpus was produced. Without it a reader cannot weigh the evidence, only accept it.

theme.description: Resolved rendering parameters. Normally derived from audience via references/audience-map.md; set explicitly only to override. The palette here is what the palette gate validates — in BOTH modes.

provenance.description: Who/what produced this IR. Honest authorship, per the agent-ticket-provenance discipline.

id.description: kebab-case stable identifier, referenced from elsewhere in the document.

date.description: ISO 8601 calendar date. Absolute always — a dossier outlives the session that wrote it, so 'last Thursday' is meaningless in it.

confidence.description: The author's confidence in THIS claim. Three bands, deliberately: a percentage invites false precision on an unmeasured quantity.

claim_refs.description: Ids of claims in claims[]. The renderer's provenance gate resolves every one of these and fails the build on a dangling reference — a chart or recommendation pointing at a claim that does not exist is worse than one pointing at nothing, because it looks sourced.

source.description: Where the claim came from. A URL is preferred but a labelled non-web source (an interview, an internal dashboard, a measurement run) is valid — what is NOT valid is no source at all.

quote.description: Optional verbatim excerpt supporting the claim.

claim.description: One evidential unit. All five fields are required — this is the contract that makes the provenance gate possible at all.

entity.description: Optional link to entities[] — which thing this claim is about.

metric.description: Present when the claim carries a number. Separating the quantity from the prose is what lets a chart cite the claim instead of restating it.

direction.description: Required for the scorecard to normalize a cell without the author having to pre-invert the number.

contested.description: Sources disagree on this. Rendered visibly — a contested claim silently averaged into a chart is a lie of omission.

derived.description: Anything the author concluded rather than observed. source_claims is required: an interpretation with no evidence under it is an opinion, and this format makes that distinction structural rather than stylistic.

scorecard.description: N options x M criteria, with evidence per CELL. Generalizes the evidence-ledger / confidence-heatmap pattern beyond qualitative UX research.

options.description: Ids from entities[]. Two or more — a scorecard of one is a profile.

weight.description: Relative weight. Omitted means equal. Weights are DECLARED, never inferred — a hidden weight is how a scorecard smuggles in a conclusion.

cells.description: One entry per (option, criterion) pair the author has evidence for. Sparse by design: a missing cell renders as an explicit gap, which is honest. A cell fabricated to fill the grid is not.

display.description: Optional human rendering of value, e.g. '208 KB'.

verdict.description: The recommendation the scorecard supports — stated, so the reader can check the arithmetic against the conclusion instead of guessing it.

override_rationale.description: Declares a judgement that deliberately overrides the weighted arithmetic, and satisfies VERDICT_UNSUPPORTED. A verdict may depart from its own grid — an incommensurable factor, a strategic constraint, a veto the criteria do not model — but only in writing. The cost is the disclosure: the reader sees that the decision was made outside the numbers, which is honest, rather than finding a grid quietly bent to fit it.

form.description: Pick from the data's JOB, per the bundled dataviz reference choosing-a-form.md — and note that stat-tile / kpi-row / table are first-class answers there: sometimes the right form is not a chart.

source_claims.description: REQUIRED. This is the field that carries the faithfulness gate into the visual layer: a chart is a rendering of claims, so it must name them.

entity.description: Binds the series to an entity so color follows identity across charts and survives filtering.

y.description: null = genuinely missing. Rendered as a gap, never interpolated into a line that implies data we do not have.

claim.description: Optional per-point provenance, for when one chart draws on many claims.

axis_truncated.description: MUST be true when y_min is set above the data's natural zero baseline on a magnitude form. The gate cross-checks this and fails on an undeclared truncation: a bar chart starting at 90 exaggerates a 2% difference into a visual landslide, and that is magnitude distortion whether or not it was intended.

truncation_rationale.description: Required by the gate when axis_truncated is true. Sometimes truncation is correct (a temperature range); saying why is the price.

emphasis.description: Entity to highlight while the rest recede to gray. Per dataviz, this is the most underused form and often the honest answer to 'make this chart clearer'.

color_job.description: Which of the four color jobs this chart needs. Drives palette resolution, and therefore what the palette gate validates.

table_view.description: Emit an accessible <table> carrying the same numbers. Default true and rarely worth disabling: Chart.js has no native accessibility, so the table IS the accessible rendering, not a courtesy.

transform.description: Declares a deterministic conversion between a cited claim's metric.value and the value plotted, so CHART_POINT_VALUE_MISMATCH can tell a unit conversion apart from a contradiction. A chart plotting 0.208 against a claim of 208 KB is honest at scale 0.001 and a lie at scale 1 — and the gate cannot know which without being told.

scale.description: Multiplier applied to metric.value to obtain the plotted y (208 KB → 0.208 MB is scale 0.001). Must be exact: the gate compares within floating-point epsilon, not a tolerance band, because an approximate scale is indistinguishable from a small fabrication.

unit.description: The unit the plotted values are in after scaling — what the axis label should say.
